UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
PLAINTIFF'S RENEWED RULE 56 MOTION FOR PARTIAL SUMMARY
JUDGMENT
Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 56(a) and
Local Civil Rule 56 for partial summary judgment on one part of Counts I, II, III, and VI of the
First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5). In the alternative, Plaintiff requests an order under Rule
56(g). This Motion renews the motion filed at ECF No. 6, which the Court denied without
prejudice to renewal at an appropriate time. ECF No. 12. A Memorandum in Support under Local
Civil Rule 7(F)(1), the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with Exhibits 3 through 5, Proposed
Order A, and Proposed Order B accompany this Motion.
THE DETERMINATION REQUESTED
1.
Plaintiff requests summary judgment on the following part of Counts I, II, III, and
VI against Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children ("NCMEC"): that
1

Defendant Katie Hall acted as NCMEC's employee and agent, within the course and scope of her
employment, when she signed and issued on NCMEC's behalf the two letters dated April 22, 2026
that appear at ECF No. 7-5 at 2-3 (the "letters").
The First Amended Complaint sues NCMEC "vicariously for the conduct of Hall
committed within the scope of her employment." ECF No. 5 9 21. Counts I, II, III, and VI each
allege that Hall acted within the scope of her employment as NCMEC's Corporate Counsel. Id. 919l
195, 216, 230, 258. The requested determination resolves the agency-and-scope component of
NCMEC's potential vicarious liability under those counts.
The determination concerns Hall's relationship with NCMEC. It does not concern
any relationship between Hall and any other Defendant. It does not resolve whether Hall's conduct
was tortious, whether any privilege or immunity applies, whether NCMEC authorized or ratified
any particular act, whether Hall performed any function described in 18 U.S.C. § 2258D, or any
count other than Counts I, II, III, and VI.
II.
THE COURT'S AUTHORIZATION TO RENEW
4.
Plaintiff filed the original motion on August 6, 2026. ECF Nos. 6, 7. The Court
denied it on August 12, 2026, "without prejudice to renewal at an appropriate time." ECF No. 12
at 1. The Order identified the filing of the First Amended Complaint and the motion on the same
day, and it stated that "Defendants' answers or other responses to the Original Complaint are not
due until August 21, 2026." Id.
This Motion does not ask the Court to reconsider ECF No. 12. It renews the
request on the record that now exists.
ILI.
THE CHANGED RECORD
NCMEC, Meta Platforms, Inc. ("Meta"), and Hall have each responded to the
First Amended Complaint. ECF Nos. 10, 21, 45. Those motions remain pending.
2

7.
NCMEC's memorandum in support of its motion states that NCMEC "responded
to the subpoenas without awaiting formal service via two substantively-identical letters signed by
Defendant Hall, in her capacity as in-house counsel for NCMEC," and that Hall "at all times
relevant was an employee of NCMEC." ECF No. 11 at 2, 5 n.2. ECF No. 11 was docketed on
August 12, 2026, before ECF No. 12. ECF No. 12 denied the original motion because responses
were not yet due; it did not address the merits. Hall's adoption of ECF No. 11 (ECF No. 45, Sept.
2, 2026) and Plaintiff's two declarations (ECF Nos. 31, 59-2) came after ECF No. 12.
Hall "adopts and joins in" NCMEC's motion and memorandum and describes
herself in that filing "as an employee of NCMEC." ECF No. 45 at 1. Hall's filing came after ECF
No. 12.
Plaintiff has filed two declarations under 28 U.S.C. § 1746 concerning the names
under which he operated Meta accounts and the reason his legal name appears in the April 9, 2026
materials he transmitted to NCMEC. ECF No. 31 (filed August 24, 2026); ECF No. 59-2 (executed
September 7, 2026; filed September 8, 2026). Both came after ECF No. 12.
10.
ECF No. 5 remains the operative pleading, and this Motion rests on it. The
declarations are offered as record evidence under Rule 56(c)(1)(A). Their consideration does not
depend on adoption of the proposed pleading attached to ECF No. 59, for which leave was denied.
ECF No. 84.
11.
The denial of ECF No. 59 is the subject of Plaintiff's pending objections (ECF
Nos. 90, 91, 102). Plaintiff also files concurrently a renewed motion for leave to file a Second
Amended Complaint. The proposed pleading retains the claims against Hall and NCMEC to which
this Motion's agency-and-scope request relates. Should leave be granted before determination of
this Motion, Plaintiff requests consideration of the corresponding issue under the resulting
3

operative pleading, following any supplemental briefing the Court deems necessary, rather than
denial solely because the First Amended Complaint has been superseded.
IV.
THE ALTERNATIVE REQUEST UNDER RULE 56(g)
12.
If the Court does not grant all the relief requested in Part I, Plaintiff requests that
the Court consider under Rule 56(g): (a) the agency-and-scope determination described in Part I,
if the Court finds that determination not genuinely disputed but declines the form of judgment
requested; and (b) the material facts numbered 1 through 17 in Part III of the Memorandum in
Support, each considered separately. Plaintiff requests an order stating which of those facts are not
genuinely in dispute and treating each such fact as established in this action.
13.
The numbered facts concern: (a) Hall's employment and the capacity in which the
letters issued; (b) the April 9, 2026 transmission and the absence of formal service before issuance;
(c) the identifiers listed in Plaintiff's Schedule A and the identifiers used in the letters; (d)
Plaintiff's account-name history, including that Plaintiff did not use "Marvelle J. Ballentine" to
operate any Meta account he used before April 22, 2026, and that he operated the Facebook
account involved in Meta's July 4, 2022 enforcement action under the name "Jay Ballentine"; and
(e) what the letters do not identify. The facts in categories (b) through (e) are material to Counts I,
II, III, and VI. Not all of them are necessary to the agency-and-scope determination. Plaintiff
presents them as alternative relief for that reason.
14.
A dispute concerning one numbered fact does not place any other numbered fact
in dispute. Plaintiff requests separate consideration of each.
V.
TREATMENT UNDER RULE 56(e)(2)
15.
Plaintiff requests that, as to any numbered fact that is properly supported by
Plaintiff and not properly addressed under Rule 56(c), the Court exercise its discretion under Rule
56(e)(2) and Local Civil Rule 56(B) to consider the fact undisputed for purposes of this Motion.
4

Plaintiff does not ask the Court to treat any fact as established in this action on that basis alone.
The Court retains its discretion under Rule 56(e)(1) to permit a party to address a fact, and under
Rule 56(e)(4) to issue any other appropriate order.
VI.
WHAT THIS MOTION DOES NOT SEEK
16.
This Motion seeks no determination concerning: the existence, contents, source,
or accuracy of any CyberTipline report; the truth or falsity of the letters' report-existence statement
as applied to Plaintiff personally; any agreement among Defendants; any Defendant's motive or
state of mind; damages; the litigation privilege; immunity under 18 U.S.C. § 2258D or 34 U.S.C.
§ 20505; NCMEC's direct liability for its own conduct; or any claim against the Doe Defendants.
It seeks no liability determination against Meta. It requests no discovery. It does not ask the Court
to modify any order concerning scheduling or discovery.
VIl. DEFERRAL AND STATEMENT OF REASONS
17.
If the Court concludes that adjudication of this Motion should await disposition of
the pending motions to dismiss or another event, Plaintiff requests that the Court defer ruling to
that identified event, whether under Rule 56(d)(1) on any Defendant's showing or under the
Court's authority to manage its docket, rather than deny the Motion without prejudice. Plaintiff
further requests that the Court state on the record the reasons for its ruling, consistent with Rule
56(a).
VIII. RELIEF REQUESTED
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that the Court:
(1)
grant partial summary judgment, in the form of Proposed Order A, determining
that Hall acted as NCMEC's employee and agent, within the course and scope of her employment,
when she signed and issued the two April 22, 2026 letters on NCMEC's behalf, and that the
5

agency-and-scope component of NCMEC's potential vicarious liability under Counts I, II, III, and
VI is established;
(2)
in the alternative, if the relief in paragraph (1) is not granted in full, enter an order
under Rule 56(g), in the form of Proposed Order B, addressing the agency-and-scope
determination and stating which of the material facts numbered 1 through 17 in the Memorandum
in Support are not genuinely in dispute, and treating each such fact as established in this action;
(3)
consider undisputed for purposes of this Motion, under Rule 56(e)(2) and Local
Civil Rule 56(B) and within the Court's discretion, each numbered fact that is properly supported
by Plaintiff and not properly addressed under Rule 56(c);
(4)
consider each numbered fact separately, so that any showing of a need for
discovery concerning one fact is evaluated as to that fact;
(5)
if the Court elects to postpone its ruling, defer ruling to an identified event,
whether under Rule 56(d)(1) on any Defendant's showing or under the Court's authority to manage
its docket, rather than deny the Motion without prejudice;
(6)
state on the record the reasons for its ruling, consistent with Rule 56(a); and
(7)
grant such further relief as is just.
Date: November 1, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
1520 Belle View Blvd, Ste. #5847
Alexandria, Virginia 22307
(407) 794-6503
jayballentine@protonmail.com
